CHIEF COMPLAINT
Pain at the end of right middle finger.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Ms. Hill is a 41-year-old female presenting with pain to the right middle finger. The patient was involved in a motor vehicle accident approximately 4-5 days ago while stopped at a four-way stop. Another vehicle rear-ended her vehicle; the driver of the other vehicle was texting and not watching traffic. In response, the patient made a hand gesture toward the other driver and struck her right middle finger against the ceiling of her car. The patient sustained minimal car damage (trunk crumpled) and denies any other injuries from the accident.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Negative except for right middle finger pain as detailed in history of present illness.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Atrial fibrillation

MEDICATIONS
Digoxin

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Recent motor vehicle accident victim.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: 41-year-old female, alert
Musculoskeletal: Right middle finger examination reveals tenderness over the distal phalanx with palpation. No tenderness noted over other areas of the finger. Otherwise examination normal.

RESULTS
X-ray of right middle finger demonstrates distal phalanx fracture of the right middle finger.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Distal phalanx fracture of right middle finger. Patient placed in finger splint. Started on tramadol 50 mg PO every 6 hours as needed for pain; 8 tablets dispensed for approximately 2 days. Tramadol confirmed to be safe with patient's current digoxin regimen. Follow-up x-ray in 2 weeks.
